requirement:
`habeas status`, and `habeas author` after it finishes, MUST report the number
of nodes without recent coverage under
{cite}`requirements.references.coverage.history`, except items inside a module
named `tests`, using the following summary:

```text
N nodes have coverage warnings. Use `status --coverage` to see them.
```

The summary MUST report zero when no nodes have warnings. Default output MUST
NOT list individual coverage warnings or coverage-history details, including
with `status --all` or `status --verbose`.
`habeas status --coverage` MUST list every warning, naming its file, line, kind,
and name, and report incomplete coverage history when applicable.
A warning MUST NOT fail validation, and repository validation MUST NOT read
Git history.
rationale:
The reviewed tests cover each obligation of `requirements.references.coverage.report`. I did not read any implementation source. Every mapping below comes from the supplied test text.

- **Summary line in `habeas status`.**
  - `tests/commands.rs#fn[status_preserves_repository_wide_rust_findings_in_every_form]` asserts the exact summary text with the count, "N nodes have coverage warnings. Use `status --coverage` to see them.", in default output.
  - It runs with no flags, `--all`, `--verbose` and `--all --verbose`, each with and without a selection.
  - `tests/coverage.rs#fn[status_shows_coverage_warnings_and_says_when_history_is_incomplete]` asserts the summary with count 2. The count is 2 because `helper` and `render` are unread while the `mod tests` fixture is excluded.

- **Summary line after `habeas author`.**
  - `tests/coverage.rs#fn[habeas_author_prints_only_the_coverage_warning_count_on_stderr]` runs `author --all`. It asserts the stderr summary with a count of 3. It also asserts that no individual warnings and no history note appear on stderr or stdout.
  - The `tests/authoring_batch.rs` tests assert the summary on stderr after a batch, after skipped-as-current runs, and after a single `--stdout` citation review.
  - `missing_keeps_current_records_and_force_reassesses_every_selected_subject` also asserts that the individual warning for `orphan` is not printed.

- **Zero case.** `tests/coverage.rs#fn[incomplete_history_is_noted_even_with_nothing_to_warn_about]` asserts the summary with a count of 0 in default status.

- **No individual warnings or history details in default output.**
  - The `tests/commands.rs` test asserts there is no "has no recent coverage" text and no "## Coverage warnings" heading in any non-coverage form, including `--all` and `--verbose`.
  - The default status in `tests/coverage.rs` asserts the absence of "history is incomplete", including for a shallow clone.
  - One small gap in rigor: the incomplete-history case is not run with `--all` or `--verbose`. The default-output path is the same code, so I did not treat this as a gap.

- **Items in `mod tests` excluded from the count.**
  - The fixture in `mod tests` is excluded from the warned set in `tests/coverage.rs`.
  - `items_in_out_of_line_tests_modules_are_not_warned_about` covers out-of-line `tests.rs` and `tests/mod.rs`.
  - `src/coverage_history.rs#mod[tests]/fn[files_declared_as_tests_modules_are_in_a_tests_module]` covers the path classification.
  - `src/rust_coverage.rs#mod[tests]/fn[a_test_without_a_test_reference_is_an_error_not_a_coverage_warning]` asserts that a bare `#[test]` is an error, not a warning, while `helper` is only a warning.

- **`status --coverage` lists every warning with file, line, kind and name.**
  - The `tests/commands.rs` test asserts the full warning text (file, line, "function", name, "has no recent coverage…") under the "## Coverage warnings" heading, in all flag and selection combinations.
  - The `tests/coverage.rs` status test asserts the same form for `render`. It also asserts that a covered `parse` is not listed, and it asserts that `parse` is listed once its coverage lapses.
  - `coverage_lasts_for_three_reauthorings_of_the_record_that_read_an_item` asserts that the full warned set is `["parse", "helper"]`, which checks that every warning is reported.

- **Incomplete history.** The shallow-clone tests assert "Coverage history is incomplete" under `--coverage` (`status_shows_coverage_warnings_and_says_when_history_is_incomplete` and `incomplete_history_is_noted_even_with_nothing_to_warn_about`). They also assert that it is absent from a complete history.

- **A warning does not fail validation.** `coverage_lasts_for_three_reauthorings_of_the_record_that_read_an_item` calls `validate_repository` while `parse` is warned and asserts that no error mentions it. The `tests/commands.rs` status runs succeed with warnings present, and the authoring tests assert that validation has no errors.

- **Validation does not read Git history.** `validation_does_not_read_git_history` removes the Git object database. It asserts that validation errors are unchanged and that `coverage_warnings` becomes incomplete, which shows that validation does not depend on Git history.

The examples `coverage.reauthored`, `coverage.new_function` and `coverage.test_module` are exercised by `coverage_lasts_for_three_reauthorings_of_the_record_that_read_an_item`. It shows `helper` warned immediately, `parse` covered through two re-authorings and warned after the third, and the `mod tests` fixture never warned.

I found no unacknowledged gaps.

`habeas status`, and `habeas author` after it finishes, MUST report the number
of nodes without recent coverage under
{cite}`requirements.references.coverage.history`, except items inside a module
named `tests`, using the following summary:
```text
N nodes have coverage warnings. Use `status --coverage` to see them.
The summary MUST report zero when no nodes have warnings. Default output MUST
NOT list individual coverage warnings or coverage-history details, including
with `status --all` or `status --verbose`.
`habeas status --coverage` MUST list every warning, naming its file, line, kind,
and name, and report incomplete coverage history when applicable.

:::{req} coverage.history
{impl}`requirements.configuration.feature_sections`
An item has recent coverage when it has a reference that covers it under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage`, or when its outline node, or
an outline node containing it, is named by file and selector in the inputs of
any version of an existing evidence record, citation review, or site review in
its coverage window. A file's coverage window MUST be its current contents on
disk, committed or not, together with its contents in each of the last N
commits in its Git history that changed it, read through a Git library rather
than by running `git`. A recorded hash MUST NOT matter here: an earlier version
names the node, whatever its code was then. N MUST be the workspace
`[coverage]` setting `reauthorings`, a positive integer, and 3 when it is not
set. When the history is unavailable, such as outside Git or in a shallow clone
missing those commits, the window MUST be the commits that are available, and
`habeas status --coverage` MUST say that coverage history is incomplete.
:::{example} coverage.reauthored
Function `parse` has no reference, and the evidence of `requirements.cli.check`
read it. The requirement is re-authored and committed twice, and neither new
record reads `parse`. With the default window of 3, the record's third most
recent version still names `parse`, so `habeas status --coverage` does not warn.
After a third such commit, no version in the window names it, and
`habeas status --coverage` warns about `parse`.
{test}`requirements.references.coverage.history`
{test}`requirements.references.coverage.report`
:::{example} coverage.new_function
A new function `helper` has no reference, and no evidence record has ever read
it. `habeas status --coverage` warns about it at once; nothing in any window
names it.
{test}`requirements.references.coverage.report`
:::{example} coverage.test_module
A helper function inside `mod tests` has no reference and is read by no record.
`habeas status --coverage` does not warn about it. A `#[test]` function in the
same module without a `{test}` reference is still a validation error.
{test}`requirements.references.coverage.report`
{test}`requirements.references.coverage.tests`
